# Appendix A: Data Sources, Processing, and Summary Statistics

## Data Sources and Processing

Code for data retrieval and processing can be found in [notebooks/data_retrieval.qmd](https://github.com/CarolynKoehn/FarmPrES-archetypes/blob/main/notebooks/data_retrieval.qmd). We used the `tidyverse` package for data cleaning [v2.0.0, @tidyverse] and the `terra` [v1.7.71, @terra] and `sf` [v1.0.16, @sf] packages for raster and vector data processing, respectively.

Census of Agriculture data was published for 1992, 2002, 2012, and 2022, so we used data from these years to represent agricultural indicators in 1990, 2000, 2010, and 2020. We downloaded all Census of Agriculture data at the county scale.

For all indicators that were simplified to principal components with principal component analysis, we retained principal components that explained >70% of the variance according to @aho2022.

### Resources 

#### Percent land in farms {#sec-land-in-farms-methods}

Land in farms and total county land data for 2002-2022 are available in the Census of Agriculture and were retrieved with the USDA NASS API [@CofAg_quickstats] using R package `rnassqs` [v0.6.1, @rnassqs]. Data for 1992 were digitized from the Census of Agriculture Historical Archive, 1992, Idaho, Chapter 2, Table 6 [@CofAg_1992_landinfarms].

#### Percent cropland {#sec-perc-cropland-methods}

Annual land cover data from the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) was downloaded from https://www.mrlc.gov/viewer/ [@nlcd]. We used the `exactextractr` package to summarize the percent cover of each land cover category in each county [v0.10.0, @exactextractr]. To calculate percent cropland, we used the sum of the "Pasture/Hay" and "Cultivated Crops" categories.

#### Percent forestland {#sec-perc-forest-methods}

Annual land cover data from the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) was downloaded from https://www.mrlc.gov/viewer/ [@nlcd]. We used the `exactextractr` package to summarize the percent cover of each land cover category in each county [v0.10.0, @exactextractr]. To calculate percent forestland, we used the sum of the "Deciduous Forest" and "Evergreen Forest" categories.

#### Percent shrubland {#sec-perc-shrubland-methods}

Annual land cover data from the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) was downloaded from https://www.mrlc.gov/viewer/ [@nlcd]. We used the `exactextractr` package to summarize the percent cover of each land cover category in each county [v0.10.0, @exactextractr]. To calculate percent shrubland, we used the "Shrub/Scrub" category.

#### Percent federally managed land {#sec-fedlands}

We used the 2023 BLM Idaho Surface Management Agency (Surface Ownership) dataset to represent federal lands [@blm_sma]. We classified the following management agency codes as federal land: BLM, BOR, COE, DOE, DOI, FAA, FHA, GSA, LU_DOI, LU_USDA, MIL, NPS, NWR, USDA, USFS. We then calculated the percent area covered by these management agencies in each county. This indicator was time invariable; federal lands are assumed to not be sold or acquired over the 40 year time period.

#### Lake area {#sec-lake-area-methods}

Lake area data is from the Hydrosheds HydroLAKES product [v1.0, @hydrolakes]. We calculated the total area in square kilometers of lakes larger than 10 ha in each county. This indicator is time invariable; we assumed that lake area would not change since 1990.

#### River length {#sec-river-miles-methods}

We accessed river data from the WWF HydroSHEDS Free Flowing Rivers Network [v1.0, @hydrosheds] in Google Earth Engine. We filtered to rivers of order 7 or lower which have long-term average discharge >0.1 cubic meters per second. Then, we found the total length of rivers in each county and divided by the county area, so that river length units are in $km/km^2$. This indicator is time invariable; we assumed that river length would not change meaningfully for this analysis since 1990.

#### Percent developed land {#sec-dev-land-methods}

Annual land cover data from the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) was downloaded from https://www.mrlc.gov/viewer/ [@nlcd]. We used the `exactextractr` package to summarize the percent cover of each land cover category in each county [v0.10.0, @exactextractr]. To calculate percent developed land, we used the sum of the "Developed, Open Space", "Developed, Low Intensity", "Developed, Medium Intensity", and "Developed High Intensity" categories.

#### Land in, nearby, and far from urban areas {#sec-urbareas}

Since the definition of urban area changed for the 2020 census, we recreated urban areas for 1990-2020 with the 2020 definitions and thresholds [@ratcliffe2022]. We first downloaded population size and housing unit count data for census blocks, 1990-2020, within 150 miles of Idaho from IPUMS [@ipums]. Then, we designated any census blocks with housing density $\geq$ 425 units/mi$^2$ as initial urban core blocks. Next, we added adjacent census blocks with housing density $\geq$ 200 units/mi$^2$ to the urban cores, repeating this process until there were no census blocks with housing density $\geq$ 200 units/mi$^2$ adjacent to the urban cores. Finally, we filtered out any urban cores without a high density urban nucleus, defined as a census block with housing density $\geq$ 1,275 units/mi$^2$, and we filtered out any urban cores with $\leq$ 2,000 houses or $\leq$ 5,000 residents. 

After these urban areas were established, land in each county was classified as "within an urban area," "within 10 mi of an urban area," "within 20 mi of an urban area," etc., increasing in units of 10 mi, with the final category being ">100 mi from an urban area." Then, we calculated the percent cover of each category in each county. This process was repeated for each year, as population growth shifted urban boundaries and created new urban areas. Then, these data were used in a principal component analysis. We retained the first two principal components, which explained 75.8% of the variance.

#### Farm density {#sec-farm-density-methods}

Number of farms and total county land data for 2002-2022 are available in the Census of Agriculture and were retrieved with the USDA NASS API [@CofAg_quickstats] using R package `rnassqs` [v0.6.1, @rnassqs]. Data for 1992 were digitized from the Census of Agriculture Historical Archive, 1992, Idaho, Chapter 2, Table 6 [@CofAg_1992_landinfarms].

#### Percent land in recreation areas {#sec-rec-area-methods}

We used data from the Protected Areas Database, which "was originally designed to support biodiversity assessments; however, its scope expanded in recent years to include all public and nonprofit held lands and waters" [@pad_us].

The following land designations (column `Des_Tp`) were considered recreation lands to calculate percent recreation land in this analysis: Recreation Management Area, National Monument, National Park, State Recreation Area, State Park, National Recreation Area, National Scenic or Historic Trail. Since some state parks were misclassified, these additional local designation (column `Loc_Ds`) terms related to recreation were added as well: State Park, Recreation Reservoir, National Recreation Trail, Recreation Area, National Recreation Area, National Monument, SREC, REC, SP, National Park, and Designated - Recreational. To capture time series data, we filtered data by date established and only included parks established before each time point 1990-2020. Parks without an establishment date were assumed to be established before 1990. We calculated the percent area covered by these recreation lands for each county and year.

#### Distance to nearest national park {#sec-dist-nat-park-methods}

We calculated the Euclidean distance from the edge of each county to the edge of the closest national park in the PAD-US data [@pad_us]. This indicator was time invariable, as all nearby national parks were established before 1990.

#### Distance to nearest ski area {#sec-dist-ski-area-methods}

We calculated the Euclidean distance from the edge of each county to the edge of the closest ski area in the PAD-US data [@pad_us]. This indicator was time invariable, as all nearby ski resorts were in use before 1990.

#### Housing density {#sec-hous-dens-methods}

Data for the number of houses in each county for 2000-2020 was downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @decennial_2010; @decennial_2020] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.6.3, @tidycensus]. Data for 1990 were digitized from the 1990 Census of Population and Housing [1990 CPH-2-14, @CofPopHous_1990]. We used total county land from the Census of Agriculture retrieved for 2002-2022 from the USDA NASS API [@CofAg_quickstats] using R package `rnassqs` [v0.6.1, @rnassqs] and digitized for 1992 from the Census of Agriculture Historical Archive, 1992, Idaho, Chapter 2, Table 6 [@CofAg_1992_landinfarms].

#### Non-federal land near major roadway {#sec-major-roads-methods}

First, we downloaded primary and secondary road shapefiles from the US Census TIGER/Line shapefiles [@tiger_line] using the`tigris` package [v2.1, @tigris]. Primary roads "are generally divided limited-access highways within the Federal interstate highway system or under state management," and secondary roads are "main arteries, usually in the U.S. highway, state highway, or county highway system" [@tiger_line_docs]. Then, we created a 10km buffer around the road shapefiles, cropping out federal lands described in @sec-fedlands. Finally, we calculated the percent of the county covered by non-federal lands within 10 km of a primary or secondary road.

#### Healthcare workers per 1000 residents {#sec-health-jobs-methods}

We downloaded data for public sector health workers from the Census of Governments [@aspep1997; @aspep2002; @aspep2012; @aspep2022]. We added local government employees in the "Health" and "Hospitals" categories. Because the first available dataset from the Census of Governments is from 1997, and subsequent Census of Governments data collection happens in years ending with -2, we used 1997 employment data for 1990, 2002 employment data for 2000, 2012 employment data for 2010, and 2022 employment data for 2020.

We used imputed values for private sector health workers for 1997-2012 from the County Business Patterns series from the U.S. Census Bureau [@eckert2021]. We downloaded data for private sector health workers for 2022 from the County Business Patterns series from the U.S. Census Bureau [@cbp2022] using the `censusapi` package [v0.9.0, @censusapi]. We used the following NAICS codes: 621111 (Offices of physicians exc mental health), 622 (Hospitals), 623 (Nursing and Residential Care Facilities), and 621610 (Home health care services). 

Population counts for each county for 2000-2020 were downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @decennial_2010; @decennial_2020] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.6.3, @tidycensus]. Data for 1990 were downloaded from the National Bureau of Economic Research [@cencounts]. We divided the total number of healthcare workers by the total population count in each county and decade.

#### Average slope {#sec-slope-methods}

We downloaded elevation data from Terrain Tiles [@aws_terrain] via the `elevatr` package [v0.99.0, @elevatr] at a resolution of 106.8872 meters. We calculated the slope from the elevation data and averaged the slope values within each county. This indicator is time invariant; we assume that the average slope will not change through time.

#### Percent change in number of farms {#sec-num-farms-change-methods}

Number of farms data for 1997-2022 are available in the Census of Agriculture and were retrieved with the USDA NASS API [@CofAg_quickstats] using R package `rnassqs` [v0.6.1, @rnassqs]. Data for 1987-1992 were digitized from the Census of Agriculture Historical Archive, 1992, Idaho, Chapter 2, Table 6 [@CofAg_1992_landinfarms].

We calculated the five-year percent change in number of farms before each time point. For example, for 2022: $(Farms_{2022} - Farms_{2017}) / Farms_{2017}$

#### Percent change of land in farms {#sec-land-in-farms-change-methods}

Land in farms data for 1997-2022 are available in the Census of Agriculture and were retrieved with the USDA NASS API [@CofAg_quickstats] using R package `rnassqs` [v0.6.1, @rnassqs]. Data for 1987-1992 were digitized from the Census of Agriculture Historical Archive, 1992, Idaho, Chapter 2, Table 6 [@CofAg_1992_landinfarms]. We used the five-year change in the percent of all county land that was in farms.

#### Percent change of cropland {#sec-cropland-change-methods}

Annual land cover data from the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) was downloaded from https://www.mrlc.gov/viewer/ [@nlcd]. We used the `exactextractr` package to summarize the percent cover of each land cover category in each county [v0.10.0, @exactextractr]. To calculate percent cropland, we used the sum of the "Pasture/Hay" and "Cultivated Crops" categories. We used the five-year change in the percent of all county land that was in cropland.

#### Percent change of forest {#sec-forest-change-methods}

Annual land cover data from the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) was downloaded from https://www.mrlc.gov/viewer/ [@nlcd]. We used the `exactextractr` package to summarize the percent cover of each land cover category in each county [v0.10.0, @exactextractr]. To calculate percent cropland, we used the sum of the "Deciduous Forest" and "Evergreen Forest" categories. We used the five-year change in the percent of all county land that was in forestland.

#### Percent change of shrubland {#sec-shrubland-change-methods}

Annual land cover data from the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) was downloaded from https://www.mrlc.gov/viewer/ [@nlcd]. We used the `exactextractr` package to summarize the percent cover of each land cover category in each county [v0.10.0, @exactextractr]. To calculate percent cropland, we used the "Shrub/Scrub category. We used the five-year change in the percent of all county land that was in shrubland.

#### Percent change of developed land {#sec-dev-land-change-methods}

Annual land cover data from the National Land Cover Database (NLCD) was downloaded from https://www.mrlc.gov/viewer/ [@nlcd]. We used the `exactextractr` package to summarize the percent cover of each land cover category in each county [v0.10.0, @exactextractr]. To calculate percent cropland, we used the sum of the "Developed, Open Space", "Developed, Low Intensity", "Developed, Medium Intensity", and "Developed High Intensity" categories. We used the five-year change in the percent of all county land that was in developed land.

#### Percent farms with net loss {#sec-farm-net-loss-methods}

Farms with net loss and total farms data for 2002-2022 are available in the Census of Agriculture and were retrieved with the USDA NASS API [@CofAg_quickstats] using R package `rnassqs` [v0.6.1, @rnassqs]. Data for 1992 were digitized from the Census of Agriculture Historical Archive, 1992, Idaho, Chapter 2, Table 4 [@CofAg_1992_netloss].

#### Agriculture support jobs {#sec-ag-support-jobs-methods}

We used imputed values for private sector agriculture support workers for 1992-2012 from the County Business Patterns series from the U.S. Census Bureau [@eckert2021]. We downloaded data for private sector agriculture support workers for 2022 from the County Business Patterns series from the U.S. Census Bureau [@cbp2022] using the `censusapi` package [v0.9.0, @censusapi]. We used the following NAICS codes: 1151 (Support Activities for Crop Production) and 1152 (Support Activities for Animal Production). 

We also downloaded the number of hired workers from the Census of Agriculture for 2002-2022 using the the USDA NASS API [@CofAg_quickstats] with R package `rnassqs` [v0.6.1, @rnassqs]. Data for 1992 were digitized from the Census of Agriculture Historical Archive, 1992, Idaho, Chapter 2, Table 5 [@CofAg_1992_hiredlabor].

Population counts for each county for 2000-2020 were downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @decennial_2010; @decennial_2020] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.6.3, @tidycensus]. Data for 1990 were downloaded from the National Bureau of Economic Research [@cencounts]. We divided the total number of agriculture support workers by the total population count in each county and year.

#### Hotel and restaurant jobs {#sec-hospitality-jobs-methods}

We used imputed values for accomodation and food service workers for 1990-2010 from the County Business Patterns series from the U.S. Census Bureau [@eckert2021]. We downloaded data for accomodation and food service workers for 2020 from the County Business Patterns series from the U.S. Census Bureau [@cbp2022] using the `censusapi` package [v0.9.0, @censusapi]. We used NAICS code 72 (Accommodation and Food Services).

Population counts for each county for 2000-2020 were downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @decennial_2010; @decennial_2020] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.6.3, @tidycensus]. Data for 1990 were downloaded from the National Bureau of Economic Research [@cencounts]. We divided the total number of hospitality workers by the total population count in each county and year.

#### Median home value {#sec-home-value-methods}

Data for the median home value in each county for 2000-2020 were downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @acs2010; @acs2020] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.6.3, @tidycensus]. Data for 1990 were digitized from the 1990 Census of Housing [1990 CH-1-14, @CofHous_1990]. We adjusted for inflation by converting all dollar amounts to 2020 US dollars using the consumer price indices for housing in December of each year [@cpiu_housing].

#### Farm size {#sec-farm-size-methods}

Number of farms in each size class and total farms data for 2002-2022 are available in the Census of Agriculture and were retrieved with the USDA NASS API [@CofAg_quickstats] using R package `rnassqs` [v0.6.1, @rnassqs]. Data for 1992 were digitized from the Census of Agriculture Historical Archive, 1992, Idaho, Chapter 2, Table 6 [@CofAg_1992_landinfarms]. We found the percent of farms in each size category available for each year, and then simplified the data using principal component analysis. We retained the first two principal components, which explained 81.1% of the variance.

### Actors

#### Population density {#sec-pop-dens-methods}

Population counts for each county for 2000-2020 were downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @decennial_2010; @decennial_2020] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.6.3, @tidycensus]. Data for 1990 were downloaded from the National Bureau of Economic Research [@cencounts]. We divided by total county land from the Census of Agriculture retrieved for 2002-2022 from the USDA NASS API [@CofAg_quickstats] using R package `rnassqs` [v0.6.1, @rnassqs] and digitized for 1992 from the Census of Agriculture Historical Archive, 1992, Idaho, Chapter 2, Table 6 [@CofAg_1992_landinfarms].

#### Population change {#sec-pop-change-methods}

Population counts for each county for 2000-2020 were downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @decennial_2010; @decennial_2020] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.6.3, @tidycensus]. Data for 1980-1990 were downloaded from the National Bureau of Economic Research [@cencounts]. We used the percent different of population over a 10 year period; for example: $ (population_{1990} - population_{1980}) / population_{1980} $.

#### Percent employed in different industries {#sec-employ-indust-methods}

Because the first available dataset from the Census of Governments, which provides a full dataset of employees in the public sector, is from 1997, and subsequent Census of Governments data collection happens in years ending with -2, we used 1997 data for 1990, 2002 data for 2000, 2012 data for 2010, and 2022 data for 2020 for all employment data.

We used imputed values for private sector employment for 1997-2012 from the County Business Patterns series from the U.S. Census Bureau [@eckert2021]. We downloaded employment data for 2022 from the County Business Patterns series from the U.S. Census Bureau [@cbp2022] using the `censusapi` package [v0.9.0, @censusapi].

The County Business Patterns data does not include public sector employees or agricultural producers. We used data from the Annual Survey of Public Employment & Payroll [@aspep1997; @aspep2002; @aspep2012; @aspep2022] to add public employees to the following categories:

- Legal: ASPEP government function category "Judicial & Legal"
- Education and libraries: ASPEP government function categories "Libraries", "Education - Elementary and Secondary Instructional", and "Education - Elementary and Secondary Other"
- Health and social services: ASPEP government function categories "Health", "Hospitals", "Housing & Community Development", and "Public Welfare"
- Recreation: ASPEP government function category "Parks & Recreation"

We used data from the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages [@qcew] to quantify employees of the state or federal government residing in each county. 

Finally, we added producer counts from the Census of Agriculture using the USDA NASS API [@CofAg_quickstats] with R package `rnassqs` [v0.6.1, @rnassqs] for 1997-2022 since the County Business Patterns data did not include agricultural production. In 2022, the Census of Agriculture began reporting on the total number of producers rather than the number of principal operators. This resulted in slightly inflated counts of farmers in 2022. We deem this to be more acceptable than fully excluding agricultural producers from employment counts in this context, but caution should be used when interpreting these data in other contexts.

We calculated the percent of workers in each category, then used these data in a principal component analysis. We retained the first three components, which explained 73.1% of the variance.

#### Percent retired {#sec-retired-methods}

We defined retirees as residents over age 65 who were not in the labor force. Population counts and counts of people >65 not in the labor force for each county for 2000-2020 were downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @acs2010; @acs2020] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.6.3, @tidycensus]. Labor force data for 1990 were digitized from Table 144 of the 1990 Census of Population for Idaho [1990 CP-2-14, @CofPop_1990]. Population count data for 1990 were downloaded from the National Bureau of Economic Research [@cencounts].

#### Average age {#sec-avg-age-methods}

Data on the weighted average age of residents in each county from 1969-2023 were downloaded from the @nih_age. 

#### Median household income {#sec-avg-income-methods}

Data for the median household income in each county for 2000-2020 was downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @acs2010; @acs2020] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.6.3, @tidycensus]. Data for 1990 were digitized from from Table 148 of the 1990 Census of Population for Idaho [1990 CP-2-14, @CofHous_1990]. We adjusted for inflation by converting all dollar amounts to 2020 US dollars using the consumer price indices for all items in the Western United States (series ID CUUR0400SA0) in December of each year [@cpiu_all].

#### Unemployment rate {#sec-unemployment-methods}

We downloaded monthly unemployment rate data from @unemployment and used the mean unemployment rate across months for each county and year.

#### Education level -- percent population with high school or Bachelor's degree {#sec-education-methods}

Data for educational attainment for adults >25 in each county for 2000-2020 was downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @acs2010; @acs2020] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.7.5, @tidycensus]. Data for 1990 were accessed from IPUMS [@ipums]. Population counts for each county for 2000-2020 were downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @decennial_2010; @decennial_2020] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.7.5, @tidycensus]. Data for 1990 were downloaded from the National Bureau of Economic Research [@cencounts].

#### Racial composition {#sec-race-methods}

Population counts for each race used by the US Census for each county for 2000-2020 were downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @decennial_2010; @decennial_2020_dhc] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.6.3, @tidycensus]. Data for 1990 were digitized from Table 6 of the 1990 Census of Population for Idaho [1990 CP-2-14, @CofPop_1990]. We simplified these data with principle component analysis, retaining the first component which explained 95.3% of the variance.

#### Hispanic ethnicity {#sec-ethnicity-methods}

Population counts and ethnicity data for each county for 2000-2020 were downloaded via the Census API [@decennial_2000; @decennial_2010; @decennial_2020_dhc] using the `tidycensus` package [v1.6.3, @tidycensus]. Data for 1990 were digitized from Table 6 of the 1990 Census of Population for Idaho [1990 CP-2-14, @CofPop_1990].

#### Farm tenure {#sec-farm-tenure-methods}

Number of farms in each tenure class (full-owned, part-owned, and tenant) and total farms data for 2002-2022 are available in the Census of Agriculture and were retrieved with the USDA NASS API [@CofAg_quickstats] using R package `rnassqs` [v0.6.1, @rnassqs]. Data for 1992 were digitized from the Census of Agriculture Historical Archive, 1992, Idaho, Chapter 2, Table 11 [@CofAg_1992_tenure]. We found the percent of farms in each tenure category for each year, and then simplified the data using principal component analysis. We retained the first principal component, which explained 92.6% of the variance.

#### Number of hired agricultural workers {#sec-hired-workers-methods}

We downloaded the number of hired workers from the Census of Agriculture for 2002-2022 using the the USDA NASS API [@CofAg_quickstats] with R package `rnassqs` [v0.6.1, @rnassqs]. Data for 1992 were digitized from the Census of Agriculture Historical Archive, 1992, Idaho, Chapter 2, Table 5 [@CofAg_1992_hiredlabor].

#### Geographical isolation {#sec-isolation-methods}

We calculated a custom county-level proxy for the Rural-Urban Commuting Area [RUCA] codes [@ruca] that could be compared across time. First, we calculated the percentage of county residents living in metropolitan (within an urban area with population >50,000), micropolitan (within an urban area with population 10,000-49,999), small town (within an urban area with population <9,999), or rural (not within an urban area) census blocks (methods for urban area designation in @sec-urbareas).

We then used the urban areas we computed (methods in @sec-urbareas) to designate counties commuted to as metropolitan (contain an urban area with population >50,000), micropolitan (largest urban area has population 10,000-49,999), small town (largest urban area has population <9,999), or rural (no urban area). Then, we used county-to-county commuting flow data [@commute1990; @commute2000; @commute2010; @commute2020] to calculate how many workers from each county commuted to six types of counties: metropolitan, micropolitan, small town, rural, >150 mile commute, or work and live in the same county. We also created two categories for residents of a metropolitan county who commuted to a county with a larger or smaller metropolitan area (by population size). 

In summary, our geographical isolation dataset contained the percentage of residents in each type of census block (4 categories total, summing to 100% of the population) and the percentage of residents with each commute type (8 categories total, summing to 100% of the population) for each county and year. We simplified these data through principal component analysis, retaining the first three components, which explained 79.1% of the variance.

## Summary Statistics
<!--
### Resources
-->
```{r}
#| include: false
#| label: "R data"

r1 <- clust_dat[["Resource"]]

r1_means <- r1 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(!c(county, year, cluster, GEOID),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "input_data_value") %>%
  group_by(input_data_name) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            median = median(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            min = min(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            max = max(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(var_name_clean = factor(input_data_name,
                                 levels = c("land_in_farms", "percent_cropland", "percent_forest", "percent_shrubland", "perc_fed", "lake_area_km2", "rivers_km_per_km2", "urb_dist_pc1", "urb_dist_pc2", "percent_developed", "farms_per_acre", "perc_rec", "dist_to_ski", "dist_to_NP", "housing_units_per_acre", "perc_non_fed_road_area_km2", "healthworkers_per_1000", "perc_farms_change", "Perc_change_land_in_farms", "cropland_change", "forest_change", "shrub_change", "developed_change", "perc_farms_w_net_loss", "ag_support_per_1000", "accom_food_per_1000", "med_home_val_in_2020_USD", "farm_size_pc1", "farm_size_pc2", "avg_slope"),
                                 labels = c("Land in Farms", "Cropland", "Forest", "Shrubland", "Federal Land", "Lake Area", "Length of Rivers", "Distance from Urban (PC1)", "Distance from Urban (PC2)","Developed Land", "Farm Density", "Recreation Land", "Distance to a Ski Area", "Distance to a National Park", "Housing Density", "Non-Federal Land near Highway", "Healthcare Workers", "Farm Loss/Gain", "Land in Farms Loss/Gain", "Cropland Loss/Gain", "Forest Loss/Gain", "Shrubland Loss/Gain", "Developed Land Gain", "Farms with Net Loss", "Jobs Supporting Ag", "Jobs in Hospitality", "Med Home Value", "Farm Size (PC1)", "Farm Size (PC2)", "Average Slope"))) %>%
  arrange(var_name_clean) %>%
  relocate(var_name_clean, .before = input_data_name) %>%
  select(-input_data_name)

###############
# get farm size raw data
# farm sizes range
# list parameters
params <- list(state_alpha = "ID",
               agg_level_desc = "county",
               year = c(2002, 2012, 2022),
               commodity_desc = "Farm operations",
               short_desc = "Farm operations - number of operations",
               domain_desc = "area operated")
# retrieve
farm_sizes <- nassqs(params)
# save a backup copy
# write.csv(farm_sizes,
#           "../data/API_data_download_backup/farm_sizes.csv",
#           row.names = FALSE)
# farm_sizes <- read.csv("data/API_data_download_backup/farm_sizes.csv")

# clean
farm_sizes2 <- farm_sizes %>%
  # remove redundant categories
  filter(!(domaincat_desc %in% c("AREA OPERATED: (180 TO 219 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (220 TO 259 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (260 TO 499 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (50.0 TO 69.9 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (70.0 TO 99.9 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (100 TO 139 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (140 TO 179 ACRES)",
                                 "AREA OPERATED: (1,000 OR MORE ACRES)"))) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(county_name, year),
              names_from = domaincat_desc,
              values_from = Value) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(total_farms = sum(c_across(`AREA OPERATED: (1,000 TO 1,999 ACRES)`:`AREA OPERATED: (500 TO 999 ACRES)`), na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(across(`AREA OPERATED: (1,000 TO 1,999 ACRES)`:`AREA OPERATED: (500 TO 999 ACRES)`,
                ~.x/total_farms*100),
         year = as.integer(year))

# 1992 data
farm_sizes_1992 <- read.csv("data/Farm_size_1925-1992.csv") %>%
  filter(Year == 1992) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("County", "Year"),
              names_from = "Size",
              values_from = "Num_farms") %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(across(`under 10 acres`:`over 2,000 acres`,
                ~.x/`all farms`*100)) %>%
  # create comparable categories
  mutate(`AREA OPERATED: (1,000 TO 1,999 ACRES)` = `1,000 to 1,999 acres`,
         `AREA OPERATED: (1.0 TO 9.9 ACRES)` = `under 10 acres`,
         `AREA OPERATED: (10.0 TO 49.9 ACRES)` = `10 to 49 acres`,
         `AREA OPERATED: (180 TO 499 ACRES)` = `180 to 219 acres` + `220 to 259 acres` + `260 to 499 acres`,
         `AREA OPERATED: (2,000 OR MORE ACRES)` = `over 2,000 acres`,
         `AREA OPERATED: (50 TO 179 ACRES)` = `50 to 69 acres` + `70 to 99 acres` + `100 to 139 acres` + `140 to 179 acres`,
         `AREA OPERATED: (500 TO 999 ACRES)` = `500 to 999 acres`) %>%
  rename("county_name" = "County",
         "year" = "Year")

# join
farm_sizes_all <- rbind(farm_sizes2[,1:9],
                        farm_sizes_1992[,c(1:2,16:22)]) %>%
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county_name),
         year = as.integer(year)-2)

farm_sizes_r1 <- left_join(r1, farm_sizes_all, by = c("county", "year")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(small_farm_perc = sum(`AREA OPERATED: (1.0 TO 9.9 ACRES)`,
                               `AREA OPERATED: (10.0 TO 49.9 ACRES)`),
         med_farm_perc = sum(`AREA OPERATED: (50 TO 179 ACRES)`,
                             `AREA OPERATED: (180 TO 499 ACRES)`),
         large_farm_perc = sum(`AREA OPERATED: (1,000 TO 1,999 ACRES)`,
                               `AREA OPERATED: (2,000 OR MORE ACRES)`,
                             `AREA OPERATED: (500 TO 999 ACRES)`))

###############
# urb areas
urb_dist_areas_r1 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/urb_dist_areas.csv") %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "dist",
               values_to = "perc") %>%
  mutate(dist = as.integer(str_extract_all(dist, "\\d+"))) %>%
  mutate(label = ifelse(dist == 0, "Urban",
                        ifelse(dist <= 30, "Within 30", "Over 30"))) %>%
  group_by(county, year, label) %>%
  summarise(urb_cat_perc = sum(perc))
```

Resource summary statistics for all counties.

### Actors

-->

```{r}
#| include: false
#| label: "A data"

a1 <- clust_dat[["Actors"]]

a1_means <- a1 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(!c(county, year, cluster, GEOID),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "input_data_value") %>%
  group_by(input_data_name) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            median = median(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            min = min(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            max = max(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(var_name_clean = factor(input_data_name,
                                 levels = c("pop_per_acre", "perc_pop_change", "emply_pc1", "emply_pc2", "emply_pc3", "emply_pc4", "perc_retired", "avg_age", "med_income_in_2020_USD", "unemployment_rate", "high_school", "bachelors", "races_PC1", "perc_hispanic", "tenure_pc1", "perc_farms_w_net_loss", "num_hired", "ruca_proxy_pc1", "ruca_proxy_pc2", "ruca_proxy_pc3"),
                                 labels = c("Population Density", "Population Change", "Employment Sectors (PC1)", "Employment Sectors (PC2)", "Employment Sectors (PC3)", "Employment Sectors (PC4)", "Retirees", "Average Age", "Median Income", "Unemployment Rate", "Residents with High School Education", "Residents with Bachelor's", "Racial Composition (PC1)", "Hispanic Residents", "Full Owned Farms", "Farms with Net Loss", "Hired Ag Workers", "Geographical Isolation (PC1)", "Geographical Isolation (PC2)", "Geographical Isolation (PC3)"))) %>%
  arrange(var_name_clean) %>%
  relocate(var_name_clean, .before = input_data_name) %>%
  select(-input_data_name)

###############
# get employment raw data
emply_a1 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/employment_industries.csv") %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "industry",
               values_to = "perc_workers")

###############
# racial composition
races_a1 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/races_all.csv") %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "race",
               values_to = "perc")

###############
# farm tenure
tenure_a1 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/farm_own_perc.csv") %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county),
         year = as.integer(year)-2) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "tenure",
               values_to = "perc")

###############
# urbanicity
urb_a1 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/urbs_plus_commutes.csv") %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "urb_or_commute",
               values_to = "perc")
```

# Appendix B: Cluster Details

Medians and ranges from county data for each archetype, including data indicators that were removed during variable selection, are reported here. For medians and ranges for each data indicator across the study area, see Appendix A.

## Resource Archetypes

::: {#suppfigb-R-influential}

```{r}
#| label: suppfigb-R-influential
#| message: false

read.csv("data/model results/drmod_resource.csv") %>%
  left_join(var_labs_R) %>%
  mutate(pretty_label = fct_reorder(pretty_label, desc(influence))) %>%
  mutate(relative_influence = influence / sum(influence)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pretty_label, y = relative_influence)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle=90), name = "Indicator") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Relative Influence", expand = expansion(add=0),
                     limits = c(0,0.15)) +
  theme_classic()
  
```

We used dimension reduction to maximally separate clusters, which is similar to principle component analysis [@scrucca2023]. We multiplied the contribution of each indicator to each reduced dimension by the overall explanatory power of each dimension, then summed each variable's contributions. Finally, we divided each variable's "contribution" by the sum of all contributions to get a relative contribution score.

:::

::: {#suppfigb-R-ranges}

```{r}
#| label: suppfigb-R-ranges
#| message: false
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-height: 8.5
#| fig-width: 8

clust_dat_sc <- list()

clust_dat_sc[["Resource"]] <- read.csv("data/model results/clust_dat_sc_resource.csv") %>%
  left_join(aoi, by = c("county" = "NAME")) %>%
  st_as_sf()
clust_dat_sc[["Actors"]] <- read.csv("data/model results/clust_dat_sc_actors.csv") %>%
  left_join(aoi, by = c("county" = "NAME")) %>%
  st_as_sf()

label_order <- left_join(var_labs_R, rel_inf$Resource) %>%
  arrange(desc(influence), pretty_label) %>%
  filter(!(indicator %in% c("cluster", "county", "GEOID", "year", "geometry")))

clust_dat_sc[["Resource"]] %>%
  mutate(cluster = factor(cluster,
                          levels = c("R1", "R4", "R5", "R2", "R3"),
                          labels = c("R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5"))) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = !c(county, year, cluster, GEOID),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  left_join(mutate(ci_clust$Resource, 
                   cluster = factor(cluster,
                                    levels = c("R1", "R4", "R5", "R2", "R3"),
                                    labels = c("R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5")))[,c("cluster", "input_data_name", "sig")]) %>%
  mutate(sig = ifelse(is.na(sig), "Not in model", sig)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = input_data_name, fill = sig, alpha = sig, color=sig)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept=0, color = "black", linetype="dashed") +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1,1), name = "") +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(label_order$indicator),
                     labels = rev(label_order$pretty_label)) +
  scale_fill_manual(limits = c("TRUE", "FALSE", "Not in model"),
                    values = c("orchid3", "orchid3", "beige"),
                    labels = c("Yes", "No", "Not in model\n(removed during\nvariable selection)"),
                    name = "Cluster mean\nsignificantly different\nfrom study area mean\n(p<0.05)") +
  scale_alpha_manual(limits = c("TRUE", "FALSE", "Not in model"),
                    values = c(1, 0.3, 0.3),
                    labels = c("Yes", "No", "Not in model\n(removed during\nvariable selection)"), name = "Cluster mean\nsignificantly different\nfrom study area mean\n(p<0.05)") +
  scale_color_manual(limits = c("TRUE", "FALSE", "Not in model"),
                    values = c("black", "gray50", "gray50"),
                    labels = c("Yes", "No", "Not in model\n(removed during\nvariable selection)"),
                    name = "Cluster mean\nsignificantly different\nfrom study area mean\n(p<0.05)") +
  facet_wrap(vars(cluster)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
        # legend.position.inside = c(0.85, 0.25),
        # legend.justification = "center")
```

Data spread of all indicators in each resource cluster, including indicators removed during variable selection.

:::

### R1

```{r}
#| include: false
#| label: "R1 data"

r1 <- clust_dat[["Resource"]] %>%
  filter(cluster == "R1")

r1_means <- r1 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(!c(county, year, cluster, GEOID),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "input_data_value") %>%
  group_by(input_data_name) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            median = median(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            min = min(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            max = max(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(var_name_clean = factor(input_data_name,
                                 levels = c("land_in_farms", "percent_cropland", "percent_forest", "percent_shrubland", "perc_fed", "lake_area_km2", "rivers_km_per_km2", "urb_dist_pc1", "urb_dist_pc2", "percent_developed", "farms_per_acre", "perc_rec", "dist_to_ski", "dist_to_NP", "housing_units_per_acre", "perc_non_fed_road_area_km2", "healthworkers_per_1000", "perc_farms_change", "Perc_change_land_in_farms", "cropland_change", "forest_change", "shrub_change", "developed_change", "perc_farms_w_net_loss", "ag_support_per_1000", "accom_food_per_1000", "med_home_val_in_2020_USD", "farm_size_pc1", "farm_size_pc2", "avg_slope"),
                                 labels = c("Land in Farms", "Cropland", "Forest", "Shrubland", "Federal Land", "Lake Area", "Length of Rivers", "Distance from Urban (PC1)", "Distance from Urban (PC2)","Developed Land", "Farm Density", "Recreation Land", "Distance to a Ski Area", "Distance to a National Park", "Housing Density", "Non-Federal Land near Highway", "Healthcare Workers", "Farm Loss/Gain", "Land in Farms Loss/Gain", "Cropland Loss/Gain", "Forest Loss/Gain", "Shrubland Loss/Gain", "Developed Land Gain", "Farms with Net Loss", "Jobs Supporting Ag", "Jobs in Hospitality", "Med Home Value", "Farm Size (PC1)", "Farm Size (PC2)", "Average Slope"))) %>%
  arrange(var_name_clean) %>%
  relocate(var_name_clean, .before = input_data_name) %>%
  select(-input_data_name)

###############

farm_sizes_r1 <- left_join(r1, farm_sizes_all, by = c("county", "year")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(small_farm_perc = sum(`AREA OPERATED: (1.0 TO 9.9 ACRES)`,
                               `AREA OPERATED: (10.0 TO 49.9 ACRES)`),
         med_farm_perc = sum(`AREA OPERATED: (50 TO 179 ACRES)`,
                             `AREA OPERATED: (180 TO 499 ACRES)`),
         large_farm_perc = sum(`AREA OPERATED: (1,000 TO 1,999 ACRES)`,
                               `AREA OPERATED: (2,000 OR MORE ACRES)`,
                             `AREA OPERATED: (500 TO 999 ACRES)`))

###############
# urb areas
urb_dist_areas_r1 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/urb_dist_areas.csv") %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "dist",
               values_to = "perc") %>%
  mutate(dist = as.integer(str_extract_all(dist, "\\d+"))) %>%
  filter(county %in% r1$county) %>%
  mutate(label = ifelse(dist == 0, "Urban",
                        ifelse(dist <= 30, "Within 30", "Over 30"))) %>%
  group_by(county, year, label) %>%
  summarise(urb_cat_perc = sum(perc))
```

### R2

```{r}
#| include: false
#| label: "R2 data"

# labeled R4 in model, we label it R2 in the manuscript

r2 <- clust_dat[["Resource"]] %>%
  filter(cluster == "R4")

r2_means <- r2 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(!c(county, year, cluster, GEOID),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "input_data_value") %>%
  group_by(input_data_name) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            median = median(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            min = min(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            max = max(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(var_name_clean = factor(input_data_name,
                                 levels = c("land_in_farms", "percent_cropland", "percent_forest", "percent_shrubland", "perc_fed", "lake_area_km2", "rivers_km_per_km2", "urb_dist_pc1", "urb_dist_pc2", "percent_developed", "farms_per_acre", "perc_rec", "dist_to_ski", "dist_to_NP", "housing_units_per_acre", "perc_non_fed_road_area_km2", "healthworkers_per_1000", "perc_farms_change", "Perc_change_land_in_farms", "cropland_change", "forest_change", "shrub_change", "developed_change", "perc_farms_w_net_loss", "ag_support_per_1000", "accom_food_per_1000", "med_home_val_in_2020_USD", "farm_size_pc1", "farm_size_pc2", "avg_slope"),
                                 labels = c("Land in Farms", "Cropland", "Forest", "Shrubland", "Federal Land", "Lake Area", "Length of Rivers", "Distance from Urban (PC1)", "Distance from Urban (PC2)","Developed Land", "Farm Density", "Recreation Land", "Distance to a Ski Area", "Distance to a National Park", "Housing Density", "Non-Federal Land near Highway", "Healthcare Workers", "Farm Loss/Gain", "Land in Farms Loss/Gain", "Cropland Loss/Gain", "Forest Loss/Gain", "Shrubland Loss/Gain", "Developed Land Gain", "Farms with Net Loss", "Jobs Supporting Ag", "Jobs in Hospitality", "Med Home Value", "Farm Size (PC1)", "Farm Size (PC2)", "Average Slope"))) %>%
  arrange(var_name_clean) %>%
  relocate(var_name_clean, .before = input_data_name) %>%
  select(-input_data_name)

###############

farm_sizes_r2 <- left_join(r2, farm_sizes_all, by = c("county", "year")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(small_farm_perc = sum(`AREA OPERATED: (1.0 TO 9.9 ACRES)`,
                               `AREA OPERATED: (10.0 TO 49.9 ACRES)`),
         med_farm_perc = sum(`AREA OPERATED: (50 TO 179 ACRES)`,
                             `AREA OPERATED: (180 TO 499 ACRES)`),
         large_farm_perc = sum(`AREA OPERATED: (1,000 TO 1,999 ACRES)`,
                               `AREA OPERATED: (2,000 OR MORE ACRES)`,
                             `AREA OPERATED: (500 TO 999 ACRES)`))

###############
# urb areas
urb_dist_areas_r2 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/urb_dist_areas.csv") %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "dist",
               values_to = "perc") %>%
  mutate(dist = as.integer(str_extract_all(dist, "\\d+"))) %>%
  filter(county %in% r2$county) %>%
  mutate(label = ifelse(dist == 0, "Urban",
                        ifelse(dist <= 30, "Within 30", "Over 30"))) %>%
  group_by(county, year, label) %>%
  summarise(urb_cat_perc = sum(perc))
```

The counties in R2 are `r names(table(r2$county)[table(r2$county)==4])`, and Gem (1990).

\newpage

### R5

```{r}
#| include: false
#| label: "R5 data"

# labeled R3 in model, R5 in manuscript

r5 <- clust_dat[["Resource"]] %>%
  filter(cluster == "R3")

r5_means <- r5 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(!c(county, year, cluster, GEOID),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "input_data_value") %>%
  group_by(input_data_name) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            median = median(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            min = min(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            max = max(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(var_name_clean = factor(input_data_name,
                                 levels = c("land_in_farms", "percent_cropland", "percent_forest", "percent_shrubland", "perc_fed", "lake_area_km2", "rivers_km_per_km2", "urb_dist_pc1", "urb_dist_pc2", "percent_developed", "farms_per_acre", "perc_rec", "dist_to_ski", "dist_to_NP", "housing_units_per_acre", "perc_non_fed_road_area_km2", "healthworkers_per_1000", "perc_farms_change", "Perc_change_land_in_farms", "cropland_change", "forest_change", "shrub_change", "developed_change", "perc_farms_w_net_loss", "ag_support_per_1000", "accom_food_per_1000", "med_home_val_in_2020_USD", "farm_size_pc1", "farm_size_pc2", "avg_slope"),
                                 labels = c("Land in Farms", "Cropland", "Forest", "Shrubland", "Federal Land", "Lake Area", "Length of Rivers", "Distance from Urban (PC1)", "Distance from Urban (PC2)","Developed Land", "Farm Density", "Recreation Land", "Distance to a Ski Area", "Distance to a National Park", "Housing Density", "Non-Federal Land near Highway", "Healthcare Workers", "Farm Loss/Gain", "Land in Farms Loss/Gain", "Cropland Loss/Gain", "Forest Loss/Gain", "Shrubland Loss/Gain", "Developed Land Gain", "Farms with Net Loss", "Jobs Supporting Ag", "Jobs in Hospitality", "Med Home Value", "Farm Size (PC1)", "Farm Size (PC2)", "Average Slope"))) %>%
  arrange(var_name_clean) %>%
  relocate(var_name_clean, .before = input_data_name) %>%
  select(-input_data_name)

###############

farm_sizes_r5 <- left_join(r5, farm_sizes_all, by = c("county", "year")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(small_farm_perc = sum(`AREA OPERATED: (1.0 TO 9.9 ACRES)`,
                               `AREA OPERATED: (10.0 TO 49.9 ACRES)`),
         med_farm_perc = sum(`AREA OPERATED: (50 TO 179 ACRES)`,
                             `AREA OPERATED: (180 TO 499 ACRES)`),
         large_farm_perc = sum(`AREA OPERATED: (1,000 TO 1,999 ACRES)`,
                               `AREA OPERATED: (2,000 OR MORE ACRES)`,
                             `AREA OPERATED: (500 TO 999 ACRES)`))

###############
# urb areas
urb_dist_areas_r5 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/urb_dist_areas.csv") %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "dist",
               values_to = "perc") %>%
  mutate(dist = as.integer(str_extract_all(dist, "\\d+"))) %>%
  filter(county %in% r5$county) %>%
  mutate(label = ifelse(dist == 0, "Urban",
                        ifelse(dist <= 30, "Within 30", "Over 30"))) %>%
  group_by(county, year, label) %>%
  summarise(urb_cat_perc = sum(perc))
```

The counties in R5 are `r names(table(r5$county)[table(r5$county)==4])`.

## Actors Archetypes

::: {#suppfigb-A-influential}

```{r}
#| label: suppfigb-A-influential
#| message: false
#| fig-cap: "Relative influence of indicators in actors model."

read.csv("data/model results/drmod_actors.csv") %>%
  left_join(var_labs_A) %>%
  arrange(influence) %>%
  mutate(pretty_label = fct_reorder(pretty_label, desc(influence))) %>%
  mutate(relative_influence = influence / sum(influence)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pretty_label, y = relative_influence)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_discrete(guide = guide_axis(angle=90), name = "Indicator") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Relative Influence", expand = expansion(add=0),
                     limits = c(0,0.25)) +
  theme_classic()
  
```

we used dimension reduction to maximally separate clusters, which is similar to principle component analysis [@scrucca2023]. We multiplied the contribution of each indicator to each reduced dimension by the overall explanatory power of each dimension, then summed each variable's contributions. Then, we divided each variable's "contribution" by the sum of all contributions to get a relative contribution score.

:::

::: {#suppfigb-A-ranges}

```{r}
#| message: false
#| fig-cap: ""
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-width: 7.5

label_order <- left_join(var_labs_A, rel_inf$Actors) %>%
  arrange(desc(influence), pretty_label) %>%
  filter(!(indicator %in% c("cluster", "county", "GEOID", "year", "geometry")))

clust_dat_sc[["Actors"]] %>%
  mutate(cluster = factor(cluster,
                          levels = c("A1", "A2", "A5", "A3", "A4"),
                          labels = c("A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "A5"))) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = !c(county, year, cluster, GEOID),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "value") %>%
  left_join(mutate(ci_clust$Actors, 
                   cluster = factor(cluster,
                                    levels = c("A1", "A2", "A5", "A3", "A4"),
                                    labels = c("A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "A5")))[,c("cluster", "input_data_name", "sig")]) %>%
  mutate(sig = ifelse(is.na(sig), "Not in model", sig)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = input_data_name, fill = sig, alpha = sig, color=sig)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept=0, color = "black", linetype="dashed") +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1,1)) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(label_order$indicator),
                   labels = rev(label_order$pretty_label)) +
  scale_fill_manual(limits = c("TRUE", "FALSE", "Not in model"),
                    values = c("orchid3", "orchid3", "beige"),
                    labels = c("Yes", "No", "Not in model\n(removed during\nvariable selection)"),
                    name = "Cluster mean\nsignificantly different\nfrom study area mean\n(p<0.05)") +
  scale_alpha_manual(limits = c("TRUE", "FALSE", "Not in model"),
                    values = c(1, 0.3, 0.3),
                    labels = c("Yes", "No", "Not in model\n(removed during\nvariable selection)"), 
                    name = "Cluster mean\nsignificantly different\nfrom study area mean\n(p<0.05)") +
  scale_color_manual(limits = c("TRUE", "FALSE", "Not in model"),
                    values = c("black", "gray50", "gray50"),
                    labels = c("Yes", "No", "Not in model\n(removed during\nvariable selection)"),
                    name = "Cluster mean\nsignificantly different\nfrom study area mean\n(p<0.05)") +
  facet_wrap(vars(cluster)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

Data spread of all indicators in each actors cluster, including indicators removed during variable selection.

### A1

```{r}
#| include: false
#| label: "A1 data"

a1 <- clust_dat[["Actors"]] %>%
  filter(cluster == "A1")

a1_means <- a1 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(!c(county, year, cluster, GEOID),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "input_data_value") %>%
  group_by(input_data_name) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            median = median(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            min = min(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            max = max(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(var_name_clean = factor(input_data_name,
                                 levels = c("pop_per_acre", "perc_pop_change", "emply_pc1", "emply_pc2", "emply_pc3", "emply_pc4", "perc_retired", "avg_age", "med_income_in_2020_USD", "unemployment_rate", "high_school", "bachelors", "races_PC1", "perc_hispanic", "tenure_pc1", "perc_farms_w_net_loss", "num_hired", "ruca_proxy_pc1", "ruca_proxy_pc2"),
                                 labels = c("Population Density", "Population Change", "Employment Sectors (PC1)", "Employment Sectors (PC2)", "Employment Sectors (PC3)", "Employment Sectors (PC4)", "Retirees", "Average Age", "Median Income", "Unemployment Rate", "Residents with High School Education", "Residents with Bachelor's", "Racial Composition (PC1)", "Hispanic Residents", "Full Owned Farms", "Farms with Net Loss", "Hired Ag Workers", "Geographical Isolation (PC1)", "Geographical Isolation (PC2)"))) %>%
  arrange(var_name_clean) %>%
  relocate(var_name_clean, .before = input_data_name) %>%
  select(-input_data_name)
```

Summary statistics for counties in archetype A1. Bolded cluster means are significantly different from the study area mean (p < 0.05).

:::

### A2

```{r}
#| include: false
#| label: "A2 data"

a2 <- clust_dat[["Actors"]] %>%
  filter(cluster == "A2")

a2_means <- a2 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(!c(county, year, cluster, GEOID),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "input_data_value") %>%
  group_by(input_data_name) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            median = median(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            min = min(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            max = max(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(var_name_clean = factor(input_data_name,
                                 levels = c("pop_per_acre", "perc_pop_change", "emply_pc1", "emply_pc2", "emply_pc3", "emply_pc4", "perc_retired", "avg_age", "med_income_in_2020_USD", "unemployment_rate", "high_school", "bachelors", "races_PC1", "perc_hispanic", "tenure_pc1", "perc_farms_w_net_loss", "num_hired", "ruca_proxy_pc1", "ruca_proxy_pc2"),
                                 labels = c("Population Density", "Population Change", "Employment Sectors (PC1)", "Employment Sectors (PC2)", "Employment Sectors (PC3)", "Employment Sectors (PC4)", "Retirees", "Average Age", "Median Income", "Unemployment Rate", "Residents with High School Education", "Residents with Bachelor's", "Racial Composition (PC1)", "Hispanic Residents", "Full Owned Farms", "Farms with Net Loss", "Hired Ag Workers", "Geographical Isolation (PC1)", "Geographical Isolation (PC2)"))) %>%
  arrange(var_name_clean) %>%
  relocate(var_name_clean, .before = input_data_name) %>%
  select(-input_data_name)

###############
# get employment raw data
emply_a2 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/employment_industries.csv") %>%
  mutate(year = ifelse(year==1997, 1990, year-2)) %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a2[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "industry",
               values_to = "perc_workers")

###############
# racial composition
races_a2 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/races_all.csv") %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a2[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "race",
               values_to = "perc")

###############
# farm tenure
tenure_a2 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/farm_own_perc.csv") %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county),
         year = as.integer(year)-2) %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a2[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "tenure",
               values_to = "perc")

###############
# urbanicity
urb_a2 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/urbs_plus_commutes.csv") %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a2[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "urb_or_commute",
               values_to = "perc")
```

The counties in A2 are Bannock, Bonneville, Twin Falls, Bingham (2010-2020), Elmore (2010-2020), and Jerome (2020).

Summary statistics for counties in archetype A2. Bolded cluster means are significantly different from the study area mean (p < 0.05).

:::

### A3

```{r}
#| include: false
#| label: "A3 data"

# labeled A5 by model, A3 in manuscript

a3 <- clust_dat[["Actors"]] %>%
  filter(cluster == "A5")

a3_means <- a3 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(!c(county, year, cluster, GEOID),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "input_data_value") %>%
  group_by(input_data_name) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            median = median(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            min = min(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            max = max(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(var_name_clean = factor(input_data_name,
                                 levels = c("pop_per_acre", "perc_pop_change", "emply_pc1", "emply_pc2", "emply_pc3", "emply_pc4", "perc_retired", "avg_age", "med_income_in_2020_USD", "unemployment_rate", "high_school", "bachelors", "races_PC1", "perc_hispanic", "tenure_pc1", "perc_farms_w_net_loss", "num_hired", "ruca_proxy_pc1", "ruca_proxy_pc2"),
                                 labels = c("Population Density", "Population Change", "Employment Sectors (PC1)", "Employment Sectors (PC2)", "Employment Sectors (PC3)", "Employment Sectors (PC4)", "Retirees", "Average Age", "Median Income", "Unemployment Rate", "Residents with High School Education", "Residents with Bachelor's", "Racial Composition (PC1)", "Hispanic Residents", "Full Owned Farms", "Farms with Net Loss", "Hired Ag Workers", "Geographical Isolation (PC1)", "Geographical Isolation (PC2)"))) %>%
  arrange(var_name_clean) %>%
  relocate(var_name_clean, .before = input_data_name) %>%
  select(-input_data_name)

###############
# get employment raw data
emply_a3 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/employment_industries.csv") %>%
  mutate(year = ifelse(year==1997, 1990, year-2)) %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a3[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "industry",
               values_to = "perc_workers")

###############
# racial composition
races_a3 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/races_all.csv") %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a3[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "race",
               values_to = "perc")

###############
# farm tenure
tenure_a3 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/farm_own_perc.csv") %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county),
         year = as.integer(year)-2) %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a3[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "tenure",
               values_to = "perc")

###############
# urbanicity
urb_a3 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/urbs_plus_commutes.csv") %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a3[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "urb_or_commute",
               values_to = "perc")
```

The single county in A3 is Madison.

Summary statistics for counties in archetype A3. Bolded cluster means are significantly different from the study area mean (p < 0.05). 

:::

### A4

```{r}
#| include: false
#| label: "A4 data"

# labeled A3 by model, A4 in manuscript

a4 <- clust_dat[["Actors"]] %>%
  filter(cluster == "A3")

a4_means <- a4 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(!c(county, year, cluster, GEOID),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "input_data_value") %>%
  group_by(input_data_name) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            median = median(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            min = min(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            max = max(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(var_name_clean = factor(input_data_name,
                                 levels = c("pop_per_acre", "perc_pop_change", "emply_pc1", "emply_pc2", "emply_pc3", "emply_pc4", "perc_retired", "avg_age", "med_income_in_2020_USD", "unemployment_rate", "high_school", "bachelors", "races_PC1", "perc_hispanic", "tenure_pc1", "perc_farms_w_net_loss", "num_hired", "ruca_proxy_pc1", "ruca_proxy_pc2"),
                                 labels = c("Population Density", "Population Change", "Employment Sectors (PC1)", "Employment Sectors (PC2)", "Employment Sectors (PC3)", "Employment Sectors (PC4)", "Retirees", "Average Age", "Median Income", "Unemployment Rate", "Residents with High School Education", "Residents with Bachelor's", "Racial Composition (PC1)", "Hispanic Residents", "Full Owned Farms", "Farms with Net Loss", "Hired Ag Workers", "Geographical Isolation (PC1)", "Geographical Isolation (PC2)"))) %>%
  arrange(var_name_clean) %>%
  relocate(var_name_clean, .before = input_data_name) %>%
  select(-input_data_name)

###############
# get employment raw data
emply_a4 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/employment_industries.csv") %>%
  mutate(year = ifelse(year==1997, 1990, year-2)) %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a4[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "industry",
               values_to = "perc_workers")

###############
# racial composition
races_a4 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/races_all.csv") %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a4[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "race",
               values_to = "perc")

###############
# farm tenure
tenure_a4 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/farm_own_perc.csv") %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county),
         year = as.integer(year)-2) %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a4[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "tenure",
               values_to = "perc")

###############
# urbanicity
urb_a4 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/urbs_plus_commutes.csv") %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a4[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "urb_or_commute",
               values_to = "perc")
```

The counties in A4 are Blaine, Cassia, Payette, Bingham (1990-2000), Elmore (1990-2000), Jerome (1990-2010), Gem (2000-2020), and Washington (2000-2020).

Summary statistics for counties in archetype A4. Bolded cluster means are significantly different from the study area mean (p < 0.05).

:::

### A5

```{r}
#| include: false
#| label: "A5 data"

# labeled A4 in model, A5 in manuscript

a5 <- clust_dat[["Actors"]] %>%
  filter(cluster == "A4")

a5_means <- a5 %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  pivot_longer(!c(county, year, cluster, GEOID),
               names_to = "input_data_name",
               values_to = "input_data_value") %>%
  group_by(input_data_name) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            median = median(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            min = min(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE),
            max = max(input_data_value, na.rm=TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(var_name_clean = factor(input_data_name,
                                 levels = c("pop_per_acre", "perc_pop_change", "emply_pc1", "emply_pc2", "emply_pc3", "emply_pc4", "perc_retired", "avg_age", "med_income_in_2020_USD", "unemployment_rate", "high_school", "bachelors", "races_PC1", "perc_hispanic", "tenure_pc1", "perc_farms_w_net_loss", "num_hired", "ruca_proxy_pc1", "ruca_proxy_pc2"),
                                 labels = c("Population Density", "Population Change", "Employment Sectors (PC1)", "Employment Sectors (PC2)", "Employment Sectors (PC3)", "Employment Sectors (PC4)", "Retirees", "Average Age", "Median Income", "Unemployment Rate", "Residents with High School Education", "Residents with Bachelor's", "Racial Composition (PC1)", "Hispanic Residents", "Full Owned Farms", "Farms with Net Loss", "Hired Ag Workers", "Geographical Isolation (PC1)", "Geographical Isolation (PC2)"))) %>%
  arrange(var_name_clean) %>%
  relocate(var_name_clean, .before = input_data_name) %>%
  select(-input_data_name)

###############
# get employment raw data
emply_a5 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/employment_industries.csv") %>%
  mutate(year = ifelse(year==1997, 1990, year-2)) %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a5[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "industry",
               values_to = "perc_workers")

###############
# racial composition
races_a5 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/races_all.csv") %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a5[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "race",
               values_to = "perc")

###############
# farm tenure
tenure_a5 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/farm_own_perc.csv") %>%
  mutate(county = str_to_title(county),
         year = as.integer(year)-2) %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a5[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "tenure",
               values_to = "perc")

###############
# urbanicity
urb_a5 <- read.csv("data/clean_data_for_PCA/urbs_plus_commutes.csv") %>%
  right_join(st_drop_geometry(a5[,c(1:2)])) %>%
  pivot_longer(!c("county", "year"),
               names_to = "urb_or_commute",
               values_to = "perc")
```

The counties in A5 are Adams, Butte, Camas, Clark, Fremont, Gooding, Jefferson, Lincoln, Minidoka, Owyhee, Power, Teton, Gem (1990), and Washington (1990).
